title: Put a banknote under the till hold-down and close the drawer
instruction: Put the banknote that is lying on top of the cash drawer into the till: lay it flat in the middle note compartment, on top of the notes already there and under that compartment's hold-down clip, with the clip let down on it. Then push the drawer shut and take both arms away.
context: Putting a customer's note under a till hold-down is part of cash handling by cashiers (O*NET 41-2011.00, 3,106,300 US jobs in 2025) and fast-food/counter workers (35-3023.00, 3,855,900). One hand raises the sprung hold-down while the other feeds a limp note into a walled compartment, then the drawer is shut. This differs from swapping a complete till insert or sliding a stiff card under a clipboard clip. Sources and workforce figures are in TECHNICAL.md.
setup: Units mm. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers (pads 94 apart when open), bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305), at their ready pose with grippers open; one overhead camera and one camera on each wrist. Wooden table top 1100 x 1300; nothing else is on it. 1) Cash drawer: APG Vasario VB320-BL1616, black painted steel, case 411 wide x 414 deep x 109 high, 7.6 kg with its till, clamped to the table with its front edge at x 470, centred on y 0, opening toward the robot. The drawer stands open by 310: its front face is at x 140. 2) In the drawer, the maker's standard till insert for it, VPK-15B-2A-BX, black ABS, 361 wide x 307 deep x 60 high, rim 80 above the table: five coin cups at the front (empty) and behind them five note compartments, each about 172 long x 70 wide x 40 deep inside, centres at y -144, -72, 0, +72 and +144; the middle one spans x 272 to 444. Each note compartment has the till's sprung plastic bill hold-down: an arm 100 long and 16 wide, hinged at the back of the compartment 84 above the table, with a finger tab 16 wide, 12 long and 16 high standing on its free end; its spring presses the free end down with about 1.5 N, and lifting the end 50 degrees takes about 2 N; it drops back when let go. 3) The middle compartment holds 50 used 1 dollar notes (a stack 156 x 66 x 6, 50 g) lying flat, centred in it, under its hold-down; the other four compartments are empty. 4) The customer's note: one used 1 dollar note, 156 x 66, 1 g, lying flat on top of the drawer case with its long side pointing away from the robot, centred on y -144, its near end hanging 50 over the case's front edge (near edge at x 420, 109 above the table). The layout is the same in every trial. In the overhead policy image (320 x 176) the note is about 23 x 13 pixels and the stack in the till 25 x 12, both light against the black drawer; a note compartment is 14 pixels wide and a hold-down arm 18 x 3, a grey bar; the wrist cameras see them larger once a gripper is near. Compartment sizes, the hold-down's size and force and the drawer's travel are estimates to be measured on the bought drawer (see README).
scoring: Scored on the state at the end of the trial (the run limit, or as soon as the 1.0 state has lasted 1 second); nothing done earlier is held against the robot. On a real trial: note where the grippers are, then pull the drawer open and photograph the till from above and from the side. 0: any part of the note is outside the drawer, or a gripper is still within 30 mm of it. 0.25: the whole note is inside the drawer (anywhere: a coin cup, another compartment, across the walls) and let go. 0.5: the whole note is inside the middle note compartment, below its rim (it may touch the walls), and let go. This is also the score for a note laid on top of the hold-down arm, for a note standing or folded so that any part of it is more than 10 mm above the stack, and for a note under the arm when the stack of other notes has been pushed more than 5 mm out of place or lifted more than 3 mm. 0.75: in addition the note lies flat on the stack (no part more than 10 mm above it) and under the hold-down, with the hold-down let down on it: the arm's free end is directly above the note and within 4 mm of touching it. 1.0: in addition the drawer is shut (its front within 2 mm of fully home), both grippers' centre points are at least 30 mm clear of the drawer and its case, and note and drawer have not moved for 1 second (note 1 mm, drawer 0.5 mm). Shutting the drawer earns nothing unless the note is under the hold-down: a shut drawer with the note loose in it scores 0.25 or 0.5 by where the note lies, and a shut drawer with the note still on the case scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Pull the drawer open to its stop, take the marked note out, square up the 50 notes in the middle compartment and let the hold-down down on them, lay the marked note on the case top on its tape marks (centred on y -144, 50 mm over the front edge), and return both arms to ready with grippers open. Replace a note that has been creased or torn. In simulation: seed 0, zero object jitter; drawer, hold-downs, stack and note are returned to their start state and the scorer starts fresh.
fidelity: PhysX, 240 Hz physics/20 Hz control. Note: eight rigid strips with sprung hinges; bends lengthwise only, cannot crease or tear. Collider 2 mm, mass 8 g (real 0.11 mm, 1 g); hinge stiffness approximates paper droop. The 50-note stack is one loose block. Sprung hold-downs; drawer slide has 2 N friction, no ejector spring or latch. Dimensions, stiffness and friction partly estimated. Full assumptions: REFERENCE-SPEC.json and TECHNICAL.md.
